title: Surface player-visible roll results for player-affecting mechanics
description:
The Claude combat playtest showed initiative and the death save to the player, but hid most other player-affecting rolls. Debug evidence showed attack rolls, damage rolls, ambush/perception-style checks, enemy attacks, and enemy damage were being rolled, but the visible transcript only narrated outcomes. This makes combat feel opaque and makes it hard for a player to trust the mechanics.

Acceptance criteria:

- Define a player-visible roll ledger policy.
- Always surface player attack rolls, player damage rolls, saving throws, death saves, ability checks when the player is aware they are attempting something uncertain, initiative, enemy attack rolls against a PC, and enemy damage rolls against a PC.
- Permit hidden or summarized handling for secret checks where showing the roll would reveal hidden information, monster-vs-monster mechanics not directly affecting the player, and hidden enemy stealth/perception when revealing it would spoil the encounter.
- Update DM prompt guidance so the primary DM knows to include the roll ledger in final narration.
- Update audit guidance so a candidate can be rejected when it narrates a player-affecting hit, miss, damage, save, death save, or ability-check result without surfacing the relevant player-visible roll summary.
- Regression tests cover: Bob attacks a goblin and misses and the attack roll is visible; Bob attacks a goblin, hits, and deals damage and attack and damage are visible; a goblin attacks Bob and misses and the enemy attack roll is visible; a goblin critically hits Bob and drops him to 0 HP in a deterministic roll fixture and enemy attack and damage are visible; a death save remains visible; a hidden ambush/stealth check does not leak hidden information unnecessarily.
close_reason: Implemented player-visible roll ledger policy, DM/audit prompt guidance, and regression coverage for visible vs hidden roll handling.
